items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: was the period of the McCarthy period.

ctx.x: Well yeah. Two flowers on a stem is a metaphor expressing the symbiotic relationship of my cultural identity as a Chinese-American and a way of honoring tradition and encouraging new ideas, new innovation. “Two Flowers on a Stem” is also the name of a work that I composed I think in the early nineties and it’s the title track of the Jon Jang sextet on Soul Note Records, which is a company that’s based in Milano, Italy and a recording company incidentally that promoted a lot of David Murray’s work. And my sextet…

was the period of the McCarthy period. And if you were a Chinese-American you were suspicious of being a Communist and so forth. I actually had an FBI investigation, but mainly because he worked for the chemical plants and so he received Q Clearance, which was the highest clearance. But anyway he died in this plane crash in 1956, a two airplane crash. And when my family tried to hold services at the Glendale Cemetery I think — was it in Burbank or Glendale — I was only two years old — they refused us services.…

It’s a nice metaphor. It must have been difficult for her to convey what that was like to you once you were old enough to understand it. Is that how you learned about the incident with the cemetery and all that, from her?
